v.why: With edge 3 absent, edge 5 is a key route to the output, and removing it can disconnect the cell (about -60 to -70 points in several runs).
Replacing avg_pool on the direct input-to-output edge with a conv gave large gains (+12 to +15 points) in several runs, more than other replacements.
If edge 3 is absent, removing edge 4 often cuts the output off, giving drops of 50 to 77 points.
Swapping a parameter-free pool on the input edge for a 3x3 conv gave consistent gains (+5 to +10 points in several runs).
Replacing a 3x3 conv with pooling on edge 2 hurt consistently across datasets, by up to -9 to -15 points.
Adding a conv to an empty edge 5 restored an output path and gave large gains (+15 to +20 points in several runs).
Replacing a 3x3 conv with an identity on edge 4 lost capacity and caused large drops of -4 to -20 points.
Deleting a 3x3 conv on edge 1 removes useful feature extraction and hurt on all three datasets, especially ImageNet16-120.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv on the direct edge to pooling consistently reduced accuracy (-3 to -30 points).
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the input edge with identity lowered accuracy on all datasets, unlike replacing a pool, which tends to help.
